# RSI Ralph

> RSI Ralph runs recursive Ralph loops. A hive of OpenHuman agents edits a copy of a folder or git branch, your scorer grades the copy against the current best, and the copy replaces the best only when a paired test says it won. It repeats until the goal is met or the budget runs out. The hive that does the editing is a package of JSON and Markdown files, so it can be edited and improved by the same loop. It ships as the `rsi-ralph` binary and as Rust crates.

Read this first if you are an agent asked to integrate, extend or operate this repository. Links are relative to https://github.com/tinyhumansai/rsi-ralph/blob/main/.

## Pick your path

- **Improve something with a score** (code, a prompt, a rubric, a config): write a loop folder and run the `rsi-ralph` binary. No Rust. This is the right path unless you are embedding the loop in a Rust program.
- **Embed the loop in a Rust program**: depend on the `rsi-ralph` crate (`crates/rsi-ralph`). See docs/library.md.
- **Change this repository**: follow AGENTS.md. Do not edit `vendor/`.

## Set up for a user

If a user pointed you here to set up RSI Ralph, do this in order and report each outcome:

1. Install the binary. It needs no `sudo` and verifies a SHA-256 before copying anything. On macOS and Linux run `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tinyhumansai/rsi-ralph/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`; flags go after `sh -s --` (`--version v0.3.1`, `--dir FOLDER`, `--dry-run`). On Windows run `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tinyhumansai/rsi-ralph/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex`. If the installer says the folder is not on `PATH`, tell the user; do not edit their shell profile unasked. Rerunning the installer upgrades. No prebuilt binary for the machine, or no network: see INSTALL.md (container image, build from source).
2. Run `rsi-ralph doctor`. It needs `git`, `diff` and `python3` for the bundled loops, and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.
3. Ask the user for the OpenRouter key if it is missing, and have it exported or put in `<loop>/.env`. Never write it into a tracked file, a commit or a report.
4. Ask what they want to improve, then scaffold with `rsi-ralph init <folder> --template <name>` (the closest of graph-coloring, math-problem, upgrade-file) and adapt the subject, scorer and brief to their task.
5. Run `rsi-ralph check <folder>`. Do not run `rsi-ralph run` until the user agrees to the spend (`budget.run_usd`).

## Run a loop (binary)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tinyhumansai/rsi-ralph/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
rsi-ralph doctor                         # git, diff, python3, OPENROUTER_API_KEY
rsi-ralph init my-loop --template graph-coloring   # or math-problem, upgrade-file; --list shows all
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...            # or put it in my-loop/.env (never commit it)
rsi-ralph check my-loop                  # validate before spending anything; exit 2 if invalid
rsi-ralph run my-loop --no-serve         # exit 0 on success, 1 when the run fails
rsi-ralph runs                           # list stored runs
rsi-ralph show my-loop/<run-id>          # outcome, spend, errors, folder of the best version
```

Always run `check` before `run`. `run` spends real money; it stops at `budget.run_usd`. Runs are stored in `~/.tinyrsi/runs/<loop>/<run-id>/` (`TINYRSI_HOME` or `--home` overrides). The best version is the run's `incumbent/` folder. Your own subject folder is never modified.

## A loop is a folder

```text
my-loop/
  rsi.json          manifest: subject, hive, scorers, decision rule, budget, epochs
  brief.md          the goal, written for the agents; may use {{incumbent}} {{history}} {{failures}} {{ideas}}
  hive/             the agents: a tinyhivemind package (hive.json, roles/, seats/, context/, constitution.json, memory.json)
  scorers/ gates/   step scripts (any language) and Markdown judge rubrics
  subject/          the thing being improved
```

Minimal `rsi.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://tinyhumans.ai/schemas/rsi/v1",
  "version": 1,
  "name": "my-loop",
  "subject": { "kind": "dir", "path": "subject", "editable": ["main.py"] },
  "brief": "brief.md",
  "hive": { "package": "hive", "lead": "lead", "wall_secs": 900 },
  "score": {
    "scorers": [ { "id": "metric", "run": "python3 scorers/metric.py", "timeout_secs": 60 } ],
    "decide": { "on": "metric", "test": "seeds", "seeds": [1, 2, 3], "direction": "minimize", "target": 0 }
  },
  "budget": { "run_usd": 1 },
  "epochs": 3
}
```

Rules that cause most failed `check` runs:

- Unknown fields fail. `$schema` and `version` must match exactly.
- Every path is relative to the loop folder, has no `..` and no absolute part, and must exist (a `git` subject's own `path` may leave the folder).
- `name` is `[a-z0-9-]`.
- `score.decide.on` must name a `run` scorer, not a judge. `seeds` needs at least two distinct values. Only that scorer can accept a candidate; judges can temper or block, never accept.
- Any model other than `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` needs a price ceiling in `budget.prices`.
- Secrets live in environment variables or `<loop>/.env`, named in `keys`. Never write a key value into a file.

Start from a bundled loop, not from scratch: loops/graph-coloring (metric only), loops/math-problem (metric plus an LLM judge), loops/upgrade-file (a behavior gate before the score).

## Write a scorer

A scorer is any command run in the loop folder. It reads `$RSI_CANDIDATE` (the checkout to grade) and `$RSI_SEED`, and either prints `METRIC <name>=<number>` or writes `$RSI_OUT/result.json` with at least a finite `score`. A non-zero exit fails that seed. Keep scorers deterministic per seed. Put the scorer and any held-out data outside `editable` paths so the agents cannot read or change them. Anything the agents must not see (held-out accuracy) goes in a `"private"` map in `result.json`. Model calls a scorer makes should go through `$RSI_GATEWAY` so they count against the budget. Full variable list: docs/specs/rsi-cli.md, "Step contract".

A `gate` is a command that must exit 0 before any scorer runs. Use one for behavior that must not change.

## Let the loop improve the agents too

The hive is files, so it can be part of what an epoch edits. Put the hive's prompts, roles, context or tool declarations under paths the subject marks `editable`, and a candidate that rewrites its own team is scored like any other. Keep `constitution.json` constraints and the scorer outside the editable paths. A hive may declare executable tools in `hive.json` (or `tools.json`) and give them to seats through `toolpacks`; the program must be on `PATH` or an absolute path.

## Library

Everything the binary does is also in Rust crates under `crates/`: `rsi-ralph` (the loop library, re-exports the rest), `rsi-ralph-score` (scorers, judges, paired decision), `rsi-ralph-evolve` (evolvers, retreat), `rsi-ralph-host` (hive runtime with typed patches, private shadow evaluation and human approval), `rsi-ralph-cli` (the binary). Public items are documented with rustdoc; run `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`.

## Contribute

Run from the repository root; CI runs exactly these four:

```sh
cargo fmt -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo build --all-targets --all-features
cargo test --all-features
```

Branch off `main`, never commit to it, open pull requests ready for review, and add tests with every behavior change. Never skip or `#[ignore]` a failing test. `vendor/tinyhivemind`, `vendor/tinybackrooms` and `vendor/openhuman` are submodules: change them in their own repositories, then bump the gitlink. Initialize them with `git submodule update --init --recursive`. Full rules: AGENTS.md.
